metaDescription: Six canister vacuums compared on motor, bag or bagless design, floor head, hose reach and upkeep, from a German-built suction machine to light bagless Eurekas.
expertTake: The Miele Classic C1 Pure Suction is the best canister for most homes with hard floors and thin carpet because it is quiet, durable and cheap to run on bags. The Eureka 3670H is the value pick for a household that wants a light bagged machine. Anyone with deep wall-to-wall carpet should look at a powerhead model or an upright instead.
introParagraphs: A canister vacuum splits the machine in two: a wheeled body that holds the motor and dirt container, and a hose and wand that you actually carry. That split is the whole point. Your hand holds a light wand, the heavy part follows behind, and the machine slides under furniture and up stairs that defeat a big upright.

The catch is that every canister decision is really a decision about the floor head, the bag and the filter. The same body can be quiet and sealed or loud and leaky, and the head decides whether it suits hardwood, carpet or both. The picks below were chosen to show those real differences.

products.name: Miele Classic C1 Pure Suction bagged canister, 6 power settings
products.description:
The Pure Suction is a straightforward machine: a bagged body, a suction-only floorhead and six power settings matched to the surface. Because the head has no spinning brush, nothing wraps with hair or scatters debris on a bare floor, and the machine glides under chairs and beds on a flexible hose.

Six power steps let you drop the suction on curtains and rugs and raise it for a threshold or a thin carpet. The body clips its own accessories on, so a crevice tool and brush are always within reach. It is built for hard floors and low-pile carpet, so a thick shag will beat it, and the bagged design keeps dust contained when you change the bag.

The running cost is bags and the occasional filter, a cost you pay in exchange for cleaner emptying and steady suction as the bag fills. Check the bag every few uses, replace the filters on the maker's schedule and keep the hose free of kinks. For a flat of tiles, laminate and area rugs it is the one to beat.
products.bestFor: Homes with hard floors and thin carpet that want a quiet, dependable machine.
pros: Six suction settings for different surfaces
Suction-only head will not scatter debris
Clip-on accessories stay with the body
cons: Ongoing cost of bags and filters

products.name: Kenmore 600 Series 81615 bagged canister with Pet PowerMate

specList.label: Heads
specList.value: 2 floor nozzles with Pop-N-Go, Pet PowerMate

products.description:
This Kenmore leans on versatility. A two-motor system, two floor nozzles and a Pet PowerMate attachment give it a head for most jobs, and its Pop-N-Go nozzle lets you move from carpet to bare floor without bending to swap a tool. A swivel head helps it follow you around corners.

The listing describes a triple HEPA filter system that traps 99.97 percent of particles inside the vacuum, which is the kind of claim worth checking against a sealed air path. Compared with the Miele it is heavier and has a motorized nozzle, so it handles carpet better and hard floors less gently. A home with rugs, tiles and a pet is exactly the case it answers.

Change bags before they are packed, because a full bag chokes the second motor. Wash or replace filters on schedule and clear hair from the powered nozzle after pet-heavy weeks. It is bulkier to carry up stairs than the lightest Eurekas.
products.bestFor: Mixed-floor homes with a pet and a mix of carpet and hard surfaces.
pros: Two motors and two floor nozzles

products.name: Eureka 3670H bagged canister, 12 amp motor, blower port
products.description:
The 3670H is the light, simple bagged canister. A 12 amp motor, a 2.5 liter bag and a body under 9 lb make it easy to carry, and a blower port lets you blow leaves and dust out of a garage or porch, which is a rare bonus at this size.

It has no powered head, so it relies on suction and a standard floor tool, and that suits hard floors and low carpet better than deep pile. The bag is a good size for the weight, but you will buy replacements. Compared with the Miele it is less refined and louder, but it costs far less and is much lighter on stairs.

Keep a spare bag set, because the machine ships with two. Empty the hose of any clog before you blame the motor, and wipe the blower port clean before using it. It is a sensible second machine for a garage or a small flat.
products.bestFor: Small homes and garages that want a light bagged machine with a blower.
pros: Blower port for leaves and dust
cons: No powered head for deep carpet

products.name: Bissell Zing 2154A bagged canister with auto cord rewind

specList.label: Floor switch
specList.value: Carpet to hard floor with a flip

products.description:
The Zing keeps things simple and light. Variable suction lets you reach low and high, and a flip switch moves the head between carpet and hard floor, which is the one adjustment most owners actually need.

An automatic cord rewind button saves the chore of wrapping a cable, and the lightweight body is easy to carry from room to room. It is not a deep-carpet machine and the bag is smaller than the Eureka's, but for apartments with a mix of bare floor and rugs it covers the daily jobs. Next to the Kenmore 600 it has fewer features and a lighter build.

Replace the bag when it is about three quarters full and check the hose for blockages. The simple head is easy to clear of hair. It is the machine for a household that wants something light and uncomplicated.
products.bestFor: Apartments with bare floors and rugs that want a light, easy canister.
pros: Flip switch between carpet and hard floor

products.name: Kenmore 81214 200 Series bagged canister, 2 motors, HEPA
products.description:
The 81214 is the entry to the Kenmore range and uses the same two-motor idea at a lighter level. Four height adjustments tune the airflow for different surfaces, and an enhanced HEPA filter system traps 99.97 percent of debris, capturing dander and dust inside the vacuum.

It is designed for the whole home, den, kitchen, car or garage, and it comes with three cleaning tools. It lacks the extra nozzle and the Pet PowerMate of the 600 series, so it is a simpler machine with fewer parts to maintain. That is its charm for a buyer who wants HEPA without a long accessory list.

Filters get washed or replaced on schedule, and the bag goes before it is packed. Check the height setting when you change floors, because a wrong setting is the commonest reason owners think the suction has dropped.
products.bestFor: Households that want a HEPA-equipped, two-motor canister without extras.
cons: Bags and filters add running cost

products.name: Sanitaire Professional Compact SL3681A canister, 10 lb

specList.label: Tools
specList.value: Two-piece wand, combo bare floor tool and more

products.description:
The Sanitaire is a commercial-rated, light-duty canister, which means it is built for janitorial closets and offices more than for a family kitchen. At 10 lb it is light, and the kit includes a two-piece plastic wand, a combination bare floor tool and other attachments.

A commercial design favours simple, repairable parts over soft touches, so it feels plain next to the Miele and Kenmore. It does not offer the filtration or the quiet of a premium household machine, but it is a clear value for a shop, a studio or a rental unit that needs a no-nonsense vacuum.

Empty the bag before it is full and check the hose connection. Parts are easy to find and cheap, which is the quiet advantage of a commercial brand.
products.bestFor: Small offices, studios and rentals that need a simple, repairable canister.
pros: Commercial rating on a 10 lb body
Four tools including a bare-floor tool
cons: Plain and louder than premium machines

buyingCriteria.explanation: A suction-only head, as on the Miele Pure Suction, is gentle on hard floors and will not scatter debris. A powered nozzle, as on the Kenmore 600 with Pet PowerMate, lifts carpet pile and hair. Choose the head for your main surface, because the body behind it is almost secondary. A spinning brush on bare floor can flick debris sideways and scratch soft finishes, while a suction-only head on thick carpet leaves embedded grit behind. Many buyers need one of each, which is why a model with two nozzles is a genuine advantage.

A bagged canister, like the Miele and Eureka 3670H, contains dust when you empty it and keeps suction steady as the bag fills. Bagless saves the cost of bags but loads a filter faster and releases dust at the bin. For allergies, bagged is the usual recommendation. Consumer testing has often found bagged models deep-clean a little better and make less mess at emptying, though a good bagless cyclone can match them on airflow. Add the cost of bags to your budget, and buy the maker's bags, since poor-fitting copies leak.

The Eureka 3670H is under 9 lb and the Sanitaire is 10 lb, while a two-motor Kenmore is heavier. A canister is dragged on the floor, but you still carry it up stairs. Pick by your staircase, not by your carpet. A canister that stays on the landing while you work the stairs with the wand needs a body you can lift with one hand if you change floors. If you live on one level, weight matters less than the quality of the floor head.

HEPA on the Kenmore 81214 and 600 series traps 99.97 percent of particles, but only a sealed air path keeps that dust inside. Look for a sealed system, not just a filter label. A leaky body defeats a good filter.

A long cord and a telescoping wand cut the number of times you unplug. The Bissell Zing's auto rewind saves the cable chore, and Kenmore listings quote a telescoping wand for extended reach. Check the cord length against your largest room.

Bagged machines cost a bag every month or two and a filter every few months. Bagless machines trade that for washable filters. Over five years the running cost is a real part of the price. A cheap machine with expensive proprietary bags can cost more to run than a pricier one with common bags. Check the bag type before you buy and note how many bags come in the box.

specDecoder.meaning: One motor drives the suction and the other powers the nozzle brush. It lets a canister run a motorized head without sapping suction.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Kenmore 600 and 200 series use it, the Miele and Eureka do not.

specDecoder.meaning: Current drawn by the motor, a rough proxy for input power. It is not cleaning ability.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Eureka 3670H lists 12 amps, a rating, not a performance figure.

specDecoder.meaning: The filter medium captures 99.97 percent of particles at 0.3 microns. It needs a sealed body to help.
specDecoder.watchFor: Kenmore lists it for the 81214 and 600 series.

specDecoder.meaning: How much dirt the bag holds. Larger bags last longer between changes.
Steps that raise or lower airflow for surface and task.

howWeEvaluated.title: Floor head design
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked whether each machine uses a suction-only or a powered head. The Miele leads on bare floors and the Kenmore 600 on carpet and hair. Match to surface was the first test.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared published weights, from the Eureka 3670H under 9 lb to heavier two-motor units. Stair carrying and swivel steering counted. Lighter bodies scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Filtration and bag design
howWeEvaluated.description: We read how each listing describes its filter and whether the system is sealed. The Kenmore and Miele claims were weighed against body design. Bagged units scored higher for dust containment.

howWeEvaluated.title: Reach and convenience
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at cord rewind, telescoping wands and onboard storage. The Bissell Zing's auto rewind and Kenmore's extended reach earned credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We read owner feedback patterns on hose kinks, bag cost and nozzle wear. Relative cost set the running order and nothing else, so no figures appear.

cards.label: Suction-only
cards.text: The Miele Pure Suction, Eureka 3670H and Zing rely on airflow. They are gentle on hard floors and weaker on deep pile.

cards.label: Powered head
cards.text: The Kenmore 600 and 81214 add a motorized nozzle. They lift pile and hair but weigh more and need the brush cleared.

howToChoose.note: Pick suction-only for bare floors, and a powered head for carpet and pets.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a light body, a telescoping wand and a grip you can hold with one hand while the machine sits below.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Eureka 3670H under 9 lb and the Bissell Zing are the easiest to move on stairs, with the Kenmore 600 as the featured option.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more on the Miele if you want quiet, durable and sealed performance. Build quality shows over a decade.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save with the Eureka 3670H or Zing if the floors are bare and the home is small. A light, simple unit is enough.

maintenance.why: A full bag chokes airflow and strains the motor. A bag change is quick and keeps suction steady.
A clogged filter cuts airflow and dust leaks through. Follow the maker's schedule.
A blockage mimics a failing motor. Check the wand and hose before blaming the machine.
Hair wraps on powered nozzles and clogs suction-only heads. Cut it away.
A kinked cable cracks at the plug. Loose coils last longer.

faq.q: Is a canister better than an upright?
faq.a: A canister is lighter in the hand and better on stairs, hard floors and under furniture. An upright is usually better on large areas of thick carpet, because its wide head and brush sit directly on the pile. If your home has both, a canister with a powered head covers more ground than most people expect.
Bagged is cleaner to empty and keeps suction steadier as it fills. Bagless saves bag cost but loads filters faster and releases dust at the bin.

faq.q: Do I need a powered head?
faq.a: Only for carpet or pet hair. A suction-only head suits hard floors and thin rugs better and is gentler.

A well-kept machine can last a decade or more. Hoses, switches and bags are the usual wear items, so check the parts supply before you buy. Premium brands keep spares for years, and commercial models are designed to be repaired, which is worth more than a feature list.

It helps with fine dust and allergens, but it works best in a sealed body. A HEPA label on a leaky machine is less useful than it sounds, so look for the words sealed air path as well, and change the bag before it is overfull so dust is not forced past the seals.

faq.q: How do I pick a hose length?
faq.a: Choose by your largest room and stairs. A telescoping wand and a long cord reduce plug changes, and a hose that is too short forces you to drag the body around corners. Measure the distance from the outlet to the far end of your longest room before you buy.
